title: Running programs
description: See what's running, run something in the background, and stop it.

exercises.task: See the programs running in this terminal.
Now see every program on the computer, from every user.
exercises.hint: ps aux: a = all users, u = show who owns each, x = include ones without a terminal.

exercises.task: That's a long list. Show only the lines about bash.
exercises.hint: A pipe (|) sends one command's output into the next: ps aux | grep <word>

exercises.task: Show the 5 programs using the most CPU.
exercises.hint: ps aux | sort -nrk 3 | head -5 sorts by the 3rd column (%CPU), biggest first, and keeps 5 lines.

exercises.task: Start sleep 120 in the background, so you get your prompt back straight away.
exercises.hint: Put & at the end of a command to run it in the background: sleep 120 &

exercises.task: List the jobs running in the background of this terminal.
exercises.hint: jobs lists them, each with a number like [1].
kill %1 stops job number 1. (kill <process id> works for any program.)

exercises.task: See how long this computer has been on, and how busy it is.
exercises.hint: uptime shows the time it's been on and the 'load average': how many programs wanted the CPU over the last 1, 5 and 15 minutes.

done: You just used ps, grep with a pipe, sort, head, background jobs with & and jobs, kill and uptime.
